L47@P2: PREFACE
L48@P2: The legal and policy framework for civil registration in Rwanda needs additional tools to ensure
L49@P2: the streamlining of the CRVS system. Civil registration laws make health facilities responsible for
L50@P2: registering births and deaths in their facilities. The laws also make the executive secretaries of
L51@P2: the cells the civil registrars responsible for registering births and deaths that occurred in the
L52@P2: communities. These officers are in addition to sector, district, and embassy registrars, who are
L53@P2: responsible for registering the nine (9) vital events: birth, death, marriage, annulment of
L54@P2: marriage, divorce, adoption, recognition, guardianship, and legitimation. These Standard
L55@P2: Operating Procedures (SOPs) aim to define the processes and procedures to be followed for the
L56@P2: registration of vital events in Rwanda.
L57@P2: A comprehensive and efficient Civil Registration and Vital Statistics System (CRVS) is essential for
L58@P2: the collection and use of information relevant to the provision of services to members of a given
L59@P2: population. When organized effectively, CRVS can play a key role for all institutions and
L60@P2: individuals requiring specific data or information. The information obtained from an optimal
L61@P2: CRVS system is essential for tracking individual births, profiling mortality and causes of death,
L62@P2: and monitoring the dynamics of key demographic indicators. These data play a fundamental role
L63@P2: in planning and monitoring public health outcomes, as well as a wide range of outcomes in other
L64@P2: policy areas.
L65@P2: Vital event registration systems involve multiple business processes and, as a result, different
L66@P2: actors are involved in the notification, registration, and certification of these vital events, as well
L67@P2: as in the use of the systems' outputs. The standard operating procedures have been designed to
L68@P2: establish clear process paths by incorporating the ten CRVS steps recommended by best practice.
L69@P2: The involvement of multiple institutions and stakeholders requires guidance on how to share,
L70@P2: produce and access civil registry information.
L71@P2: We hope that the SOPs will provide the necessary procedures and requirements to secure the
L72@P2: services produced in the CRVS system, eliminate unnecessary bureaucracy, and achieve optimal
L73@P2: functioning of the CRVS in compliance with Rwandan laws and international best practices.
L74@P2: MUKESHA Josephine
L75@P2: DIRECTOR GENERAL

L77@P3: ACKNOWLEDGEMENTS
L78@P3: The National Identification Agency, on behalf of the national CRVS stakeholders, would like to
L79@P3: thank all the organizations and individuals who have contributed to the development and
L80@P3: updating of these standard operating procedures for the management of civil status registration
L81@P3: in Rwanda.
L82@P3: This document is a result of the great collaboration that exists between the National
L83@P3: Identification Agency and various stakeholders who are dedicated to creating a positive change
L84@P3: in the Rwandan civil registration landscape. Special appreciation goes to World Health
L85@P3: Organization (WHO) who provided funding for the consultancy services for this document to be
L86@P3: developed.
L87@P3: We appreciate all the efforts invested in the development of the current Civil Registration
L88@P3: Standard Operating Procedures. Implementation and monitoring of these guidelines will
L89@P3: contribute to the sector’s common goal of building a stronger CRVS systems that is driven by
L90@P3: ensuring that everyone is recognized and count.

L58@P4: Auditor-General’s overview
L59@P4: E ngā mana, e ngā reo, e ngā karangarangatanga maha o te motu, tēnā koutou.
L60@P4: Immigration has played, and continues to play, a significant role in shaping New
L61@P4: Zealand socially, culturally, and economically. Ensuring that the country has people
L62@P4: with the skills needed to support communities to thrive is an important function
L63@P4: of a modern immigration system.
L64@P4: Skilled residence visa applications make up a small proportion of the total number
L65@P4: of visa applications processed each year, but these applicants are a strategically
L66@P4: important group who are in demand internationally. It is important that these
L67@P4: applicants’ experiences of applying for visas are well-managed because skilled
L68@P4: residence visa systems can give countries a competitive edge in the global skills
L69@P4: market.
L70@P4: Effective visa systems are timely, clear, and fair. They give confidence to migrants,
L71@P4: to the public, and to employers who need the skills that migrants bring.
L72@P4: This means that alongside its role to process visa applications and manage
L73@P4: immigration risks, Immigration New Zealand can influence skilled migrants’
L74@P4: decisions about whether to live and work here.
L75@P4: Given the importance of skilled migrants and the number of recent changes to
L76@P4: the skilled residence visa system, I wanted to see how well Immigration New
L77@P4: Zealand, which is part of the Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment,
L78@P4: manages how it makes decisions about whether to grant skilled residence visas.
L79@P4: I particularly wanted to know how well the process works for applicants, who are
L80@P4: likely to have many countries to choose from when deciding where to settle.
L81@P4: I also wanted to know how well Immigration New Zealand communicates its
L82@P4: performance. Regular, relevant reporting promotes an understanding of how
L83@P4: well the immigration system is working and can inform longer-term workforce
L84@P4: planning and policy.
L85@P4: What we found
L86@P4: Immigration New Zealand has been taking steps to provide better information
L87@P4: and support for applicants across the wide range of visas that it processes. This
L88@P4: programme of work is in its early stages, but we saw a strong commitment by
L89@P4: Immigration New Zealand to improving the experience of its applicants and to
L90@P4: managing the quality of decision-making.
